segments.title: Chương 311: 0313 [Kế hoạch 18 vĩ đại]
segments.content:
In the year 2000, *Fate of the Dragon* was showcased at the E3 Expo and secured a global distribution deal with a foreign company, becoming the first Chinese game to break into the GLOBAL100 list.

At the time, it hadn't even won any awards yet. Just this news alone, upon reaching China, was enough to make countless countrymen cheer with joy. It was then released in mainland China, and its first-day sales exceeded 100,000 copies!

Because of the century of humiliation, the Chinese people had long lacked a certain kind of confidence.

When a foreigner praised a domestic product, everyone would assume it must be excellent, and their sense of national pride would instantly soar.

The same thing happened with King Hu's *A Touch of Zen* back in the day.

When it premiered in Taiwan, the box office was a disaster. Only the first part was even shown; the second was cut by the cinemas. It took another two full years before the second part was released.

Five years after filming was completed, *A Touch of Zen* won an award at Cannes.

It became famous overnight. The two parts were quickly condensed and re-edited, and upon its re-release in Taiwan, it made a fortune at the box office!

When the news of *Seven Nights* winning an award at Cannes came back, its sales shot up by more than 5,000 copies on the first day. On the second day, as the news spread further, its single-day sales directly broke the 10,000-copy mark.

Immediately after, word-of-mouth for the game began to spread. Everyone who played it said it was incredible.

And so, its single-day sales soared to 40,000 copies.

This was also thanks to the game's multi-platform compatibility. As long as the hardware could handle it, anyone could play *Seven Nights*, the only difference being the graphics.

If that Korean game had won the award, players wouldn't have been able to play it even if they wanted to buy it; it was only compatible with high-end phones. That's why that shoddy Korean company later went bankrupt.

Shanghai, Shanda.

Chen Tianqiao was playing *Seven Nights*. He liked the game a lot. It had substance, and after beating it, it prompted one to reflect on life.

The reason he had noticed it so quickly was because Chen Tianqiao, in order to keep up with industry trends, was a regular reader of the *China Computer News*.

Ever since the failure of the Shanda Box, Chen Tianqiao had been busy transforming his business.

Shifting from a focus on licensing to a focus on in-house development, and expanding from PC games to mobile games. He had also released *The World of Legend Mobile* last year, and he had just acquired a gaming company in Chengdu.

The company Chen Tianqiao acquired was Chengdu Jintian Technology, with an investment exceeding 100 million RMB!

The 23-year-old entrepreneur, surnamed Peng, was a rich second-generation kid from Chengdu who had become a Canadian citizen. By selling his company, he instantly became a hundred-millionaire. And this year he started another company, which he would also sell to Shanda next year for another 140 million.

Chen Guiliang's investment was in Chengdu Dingguo Technology, a pitiful sum that could only be measured in the millions.

Comparing the two, Chen Tianqiao was far more dominant.

The profits from Jintian Technology's *Fengyun Online* and *Legend Online* could definitely crush *Seven Nights*. Even *The World of Legend Mobile* could crush *Seven Nights* in terms of profit.

But Chen Tianqiao just didn't feel right!

He had no shortage of money-making games. What he lacked was a game with the intellectual and cultural depth of *Seven Nights*.

Chen Tianqiao called over the head of the "18 Plan" and said, "In the future, when screening entrepreneurs, don't just look at market potential. You also need to see if the game itself has value! I'm talking about cultural value, about the company's reputation!"

The project head wanted to say something but held his tongue. Facing his boss, he could only agree.

The so-called "18 Plan" meant that on the 18th of every month, all Shanda executives, including Chen Tianqiao, would put aside their work to listen to entrepreneurs pitch their stories. If a startup project had value, Shanda would invest.

But it was impossible to let a swarm of entrepreneurs rush in. Who would present this month and who would present next month required an initial screening by the person in charge.

And how did this person screen them?

Naturally, he chose those that sounded reliable and capable of making a lot of money.

They barely even looked at standalone PC games, let alone the even more niche standalone mobile games!

The project head left, trembling with fear. He didn't dare speak the truth: Tang Kai had sent an email to the "18 Plan" inbox at the end of last year. At the time, he mentioned *Seven Nights* and *Path to the Underworld*, and also talked about developing a proprietary 3D mobile game engine.

The project head had thought it was unreliable from the get-go. No money, yet developing two games at once, and spouting nonsense about a proprietary 3D mobile game engine. He had directly dismissed Tang Kai as a scammer!

Ever since Shanda announced the "18 Plan," there had been many such scammers, and screening projects was a huge headache for him.

Chen Tianqiao leaned back in his boss's chair, a cigarette between his lips, staring at his phone screen.

He wished *Seven Nights* was a game under his own company.

If it were his, he could show it off everywhere. Not to show off how much money it made, but to show off that his company's games also had depth and substance.

Besides the "18 Plan" to support entrepreneurs, Shanda also had the "20 Plan" to encourage the creation of high-quality games.

He had organized the company's internal development teams into independent units. If an in-house game succeeded, the team would get a 20% cut.

20% of the game's revenue, given directly to the development team. This drove everyone in Shanda's game department crazy.

But it seemed it wasn't an entirely positive stimulus.

It also brought negative consequences!

The leaders of each development team racked their brains thinking about how to embed payment systems. The teams were riddled with conflict as they fought over development resources. They even tried to schmooze and build connections with the operations team, all just to get more operational resources allocated to them...

Under the stimulus of the 20% cut, what the project leaders thought about wasn't how to make a high-quality game. It was how to get their game online quickly and get their hands on that revenue share.

What? Take your time to build a masterpiece?

Are you out of your mind?

You had to get the game out quickly, get that money in hand. What if the boss changed his mind one day?

Besides, a masterpiece polished over two or three years wasn't necessarily more profitable than a shoddily made one.

Chen Tianqiao thought he was being very sincere, thought that this would produce high-quality games, but he never expected things to go in the exact opposite direction.

Every time he went for an inspection, he saw development teams with high morale, and heard that such-and-such project was being meticulously crafted.

The next day, it was the 18th again.

All the Shanda executives accompanied Chen Tianqiao to listen to entrepreneurs pitch their stories.

"Hello to all the senior leaders of Shanda," a young man began, "My name is Zhu Zhihao, founder of Shanghai Youqu... I hope to purchase the game adaptation rights for *Ghost Blows Out the Light*..."

"Wait!"

The screening head of the "18 Plan" said, "The material you submitted doesn't seem to be about this story, does it?"

Zhu Zhihao said with a long face, "CEO Chen, please just do me a favor and sell me *Ghost Blows Out the Light*. Starting a business isn't easy for me. I finally managed to start a company, and then I got scammed buying the rights to *Ghost Blows Out the Light*!"

Chen's younger brother asked curiously, "How did you get scammed?"

Zhu Zhihao looked like his mother had just died. "There's a company called Mancheng that claimed to have the full rights to *Ghost Blows Out the Light*. I spent 2 million to buy the game adaptation rights, only to find out later that they only had the manga adaptation rights for the first book of *Ghost Blows Out the Light*, and had no authority to sub-license the game adaptation rights. But my game is already in development!"

Upon hearing this, the Shanda executives couldn't help but chuckle, and some even laughed out loud.

They had never seen such a stupid entrepreneur, who could even screw up buying game rights.

Chen Tianqiao asked, "How far along is your game?"

Zhu Zhihao said, "The team has been in place for a while, the game content plan is done, and the character concept art is basically all drawn... If Shanda doesn't sell me the rights, my only option is to jump off a building. I can't possibly pay back the startup money!"

Chen Tianqiao carefully reviewed the game design document for *Ghost Blows Out the Light*, looked at the character concept art, and nodded. "This is not bad. It's a 3D game, right? I can sell you the 3D game rights for the first book of *Ghost Blows Out the Light*. Remember, it's limited to the 3D game rights for the first book. You are not allowed to make content from the second book, nor are you allowed to make a 2D online game, a standalone game, or a mobile game. A flat price of 5 million."

Zhu Zhihao's expression remained desperate. "If I spend 5 million on the rights, I won't have a single cent left. How am I supposed to develop the game? How about we sign an agreement to pay the licensing fee after the game goes online."
